title: Navigating the AWS Management Console 🧭
description: Get comfortable with the console layout, search, and region selector.

slides.title: Welcome to the Console 🖥️
slides.content:
# Your Dashboard

After login, you land on the **AWS Management Console** home page. Key areas:
- **Top bar**: Services search, region selector, account dropdown.
- **Recently visited services**: Quick links.
- **AWS Health**: Any issues affecting your resources.
- **Cost and usage**: Quick summary (update delayed by ~24h).

It may look overwhelming with 200+ services – you’ll pin your favourites soon.

quizData.question: Where in the console do you switch the AWS Region you’re working in?

options.text: Top‑right corner, next to your account name
It’s set during sign‑up and cannot be changed

quizData.explanation: The region selector is a dropdown in the top navigation bar, usually showing the current region (e.g., N. Virginia). Changing it affects the resources you see.

slides.title: The Services Menu 🔍
slides.content:
# Find What You Need

- Click **Services** (or type into the search bar).
- Services are grouped by category: Compute, Storage, Database, etc.
- Use the **star icon** ⭐ to pin frequently used services to the top navigation.

**Try this**: Search “EC2” – you’ll see both the service and its features. Pin it by clicking the star.

slides.title: Global vs Regional Services 🌐
slides.content:
# Not All Services Are Regional

Some services are **global** – they don’t require region selection (e.g., IAM, Route 53, CloudFront).

Others are **regional** – you must pick a region (e.g., EC2, S3, RDS).

**Why it matters**: If you switch regions, you won’t see resources from another region. A common beginner mistake: “I launched an EC2 instance but can’t see it!” – check the region selector.

quizData.question: Which of the following is a global service?
quizData.explanation: IAM is global – you create users once and they work across all regions. S3 is a bit special: bucket names are globally unique, but you store data in a chosen region.

slides.title: Pro Tip: Bookmark the Console 🚀
slides.content:
## Sign‑in URLs

- Root user sign‑in: `https://console.aws.amazon.com/`
- IAM user sign‑in: A custom URL like `https://your-alias.signin.aws.amazon.com/console`

Bookmark the IAM user sign‑in page – you’ll use it daily.
